title: Server-obtainable quoted runtime observation for Claude pin requests
description:
MEASURED GAP (2026-08-16, at commit 66ae6ef, by grep + a real Windows run). createClaudeRuntimePinRequest (task-75ee4a84) mints fs/facts/clock from three plain data fields, but NOTHING in the shipped public surface can produce the `quotedObservation` it validates against, so no consumer can reach a PROVEN Claude launch.

Symbol by symbol, all in packages/runner/src/surface/claude-surface.ts:85-92 (explicitly WITHHELD): `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime`, `probeClaudeRuntime`, `createNodeClaudeRuntimeFs`, `ClaudeRuntimeFactsPort`. Also internal: `capabilitySchemaDigestOf` (packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-capabilities.ts:273) and `canonicalDigest`. Public `buildProviderRuntimeObservation` accepts caller-claimed `reportedVersion` and `adapterCapabilitySchemaDigest`, and prepareClaudeRuntimePin compares exactly those two plus platformIdentity (claude-runtime-pin.ts factsDigest, lines 130-141).

REPRODUCED on real Windows 10.0.26200 through apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts against the genuinely installed claude.exe 2.1.233: a self-assembled quote whose closure hash and paths are all TRUE is still refused CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_CHANGED@RUNTIME, because the capability schema digest and reported version can only come from an observation the runner made itself. A stand-in binary refuses CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID@RUNTIME after the shipped broker really ran its --version probe.

Consequence: task-6cbff010's dispatch service composes the real launcher correctly and persists honest SUSPECT/UNKNOWN advisories, but the PROVEN branch (grant consumed -> PREFLIGHT/STARTED registration -> result manifest) cannot be exercised end to end by any consumer, and MUST NOT be faked by reimplementing the digest authority in a test.

NEEDED: a bare-root capability that RETURNS a quoted ProviderRuntimeObservation for the installed runtime without handing the caller an executablePath-steerable observer — e.g. a discovery step that resolves the installed Claude itself and answers {observation} (or a durable host-capability record the activation path can carry), preserving the asymmetry task-75ee4a84 deliberately created. Consumers: task-6cbff010 (acceptance), the Foundation ingress chain (task-a9fd91c3) and task-44d48.
definitionOfDone: A bare-root @moe/runner capability answers a quoted ProviderRuntimeObservation for the installed Claude runtime without accepting a caller-named executablePath, filesystem, facts port or clock.

createClaudeRuntimePinRequest accepts that observation and prepareClaudeRuntimePin reaches a PROVEN pin against the really installed binary on Windows, proven by a real launch, not by a rebuilt digest.
Every refusal keeps the exact code and layer of the authority that answered; a quote no production observation minted stays refused with CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_CHANGED.

apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts can be extended to a real PROVEN dispatch (grant consumed, PREFLIGHT then STARTED registration, result manifest persisted) with no test-owned capability.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE AND CONFIRM THE GAP — it is real, precisely measured by whoever filed this, and it is the direct consequence of an asymmetry task-75ee4a84 created on purpose. Re-verify at current HEAD (measured at 81a9f30).
`claude-surface.ts` states the asymmetry and its reason verbatim: "WITHHELD, and the asymmetry is the whole deliverable: `createNodeClaudeRuntimeFs`, `RUNTIME_PIN_CHUNK_BYTES`, `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime`, `probeClaudeRuntime`, `ClaudeRuntimeFsPort`, `ClaudeRuntimeFactsPort` and `ClaudeRuntimeObservationRefused` all stay internal. Publishing any one of them would re-open the injectable seam this factory exists to close — `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` most of all, because it takes an `executablePath` and a consumer holding it could point the host observer at a binary no quote ever committed to."
That reasoning is CORRECT and must survive this task. What it left missing is the other half: nothing public can produce the `quotedObservation` the factory validates against, so no consumer can reach a PROVEN launch.
WHY A SELF-ASSEMBLED QUOTE CANNOT WORK, and the measurement that proves it is not a bug to route around: `factsDigest` (claude-runtime-pin.ts:130-141) compares exactly `reportedVersion`, `adapterCapabilitySchemaDigest` and `platformIdentity{os,arch,osVersion}` — with the comment "Compares only what the runtime IS, so pinned paths may legitimately differ." The version and the capability digest can only come from an observation the runner made itself, which is why the filer's real-Windows run refused a quote whose closure hash and paths were all TRUE with `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_CHANGED@RUNTIME`. Reproduce that refusal yourself before building; it is the spec.
NO EXISTING PUBLIC RESOLUTION: `claude-launch-selection.ts` is about launch flags, model and reasoning effort, is not published from the surface, and resolves no executable. So discovery is genuinely new.
GATES, each separate with its own exit code — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test`, recording count lines and every failing file as your before-set.

TDD RED — the discovery contract, whose whole job is to be UNSTEERABLE. Create the test against the not-yet-existing capability.
THE SHAPE: a bare-root function that takes NO caller-named executable path, filesystem, facts port or clock — ideally no arguments beyond bounded options that cannot select a binary — resolves the installed Claude runtime from the HOST itself, observes it through the withheld `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime`, and answers `{observation}` or an existing stable refusal. The asymmetry is preserved because the caller cannot say WHICH binary; the host answers that.
PIN THE UNSTEERABILITY AS A TYPE-LEVEL FACT, not a runtime check: assert there is no parameter, overload, optional field or exported type through which a caller could supply an executable path, an fs, a facts port or a clock. A runtime rejection is one refactor from being relaxed; an absent parameter is not.
RESOLUTION MUST REFUSE AMBIGUITY. If host resolution finds ZERO candidates, refuse. If it finds MORE THAN ONE, refuse — never pick the first. A caller who can influence the host's candidate set (PATH order, a shadowing install) must not be able to steer the observation by making one candidate win; refusing ambiguity is what removes that lever. Pin both with exact code and layer.
REFUSALS PASS THROUGH UNCHANGED. `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` answers with four arms — an observed record, a `ClaudeRuntimePinFailure`, a `ClaudeFailure<ClaudeObservationErrorCode>`, or a `WindowsProcessUnknown`. Each keeps its own code AND the layer of the authority that answered; do not restamp them into a discovery vocabulary, because four layers can answer here and restamping erases which did (DoD 3).
AND THE NEGATIVE SURFACE: assert the root still does NOT publish `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime`, `probeClaudeRuntime`, `createNodeClaudeRuntimeFs`, `ClaudeRuntimeFsPort` or `ClaudeRuntimeFactsPort`. Assert against the imported NAMESPACE, not the file text — the barrel can re-export via `export *`, which a grep cannot see through.

IMPLEMENT THE DISCOVERY CAPABILITY. Create `claude-runtime-discovery.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./claude-runtime-discovery.ts";`, LF ending — the bridge guard byte-compares).
HOST RESOLUTION, and keep it narrow: resolve candidates from the host's own configuration — the PATH entries and the platform's known install locations — canonicalising each and de-duplicating by real path before counting, so one binary reachable two ways is one candidate rather than an ambiguity refusal. Exactly one surviving candidate proceeds; zero or many refuse. Do NOT accept a hint, an override, or an environment variable a caller could set to choose — that would reintroduce the steerability the withheld comment exists to prevent, in a new costume.
Then call the withheld `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` with the resolved path and the installed root derived from it, and return its observation unchanged. This module is the ONLY thing that may hold that function's `executablePath` argument, and it hands it a path no caller chose.
ERROR MESSAGES MUST NOT ECHO the resolved path, argv, environment values or digests — task-32eddfd3 was QA-rejected once on exactly that rail, and a discovery refusal naming the paths it searched would leak the host layout to any caller who can trigger one.
Keep the file under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts). Do NOT modify `claude-host-runtime.ts`, `claude-runtime-pin.ts` or `claude-runtime-request.ts` — they belong to landed tasks; this is additive.

PUBLISH IT, AND REWRITE THE ASYMMETRY COMMENT SO IT STAYS TRUE. Add the discovery function and the result/refusal types a consumer needs to `packages/runner/src/surface/claude-surface.ts`, and update `packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts`, which pins the root export list and its exact length — a bare addition fails until the fixture is updated, and that failure is the fixture working.
THE COMMENT IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE. The existing WITHHELD paragraph explains that `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` stays internal "because it takes an `executablePath` and a consumer holding it could point the host observer at a binary no quote ever committed to." That reason still holds and must remain — but the paragraph now also has to say what IS published and why publishing it does not re-open the seam: the discovery capability names no binary, so a consumer can obtain an observation of THE installed runtime without being able to choose WHICH runtime gets observed. Write that distinction explicitly. A future reader who sees an observation-returning function on the root and no explanation will reasonably conclude the withholding was abandoned.
Keep every existing withheld name withheld. The negative surface assertions from step 2 must still pass, and step 6's drill re-proves they read the namespace rather than the file text.
Measure `claude-surface.ts` after editing with `grep -c ''` — it was 212 lines before the pin-request task added to it, so confirm it is still under the 250 target and split the export block into a sibling surface module rather than compressing if it is not.

THE REAL-WINDOWS PROOF — DoD 2, and the only thing that distinguishes this from a shape exercise. On a real Windows host with the genuinely installed claude.exe, drive the whole round trip: discovery answers an observation, `createClaudeRuntimePinRequest` accepts it, and `prepareClaudeRuntimePin` reaches a PROVEN pin. Assert PROVEN, and assert it came from a REAL LAUNCH — the shipped broker actually ran its `--version` probe — not from a rebuilt digest. The filer proved the negative on this exact hardware (claude.exe 2.1.233, Windows 10.0.26200); this is the positive that closes it.
ASSERT THE ROUND TRIP BINDS, both directions: the quoted observation's `reportedVersion`, `adapterCapabilitySchemaDigest` and `platformIdentity` survive into the pin — those are exactly what `factsDigest` compares — while the pinned closure paths may legitimately differ, per that function's own comment. A test asserting whole-object equality would fail for the wrong reason and then get "fixed" by loosening the assertion that matters.
AND KEEP THE NEGATIVE (DoD 3): a self-assembled quote that no production observation minted still refuses `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_CHANGED` at `RUNTIME`, and a stand-in binary still refuses `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID` at `RUNTIME` after the broker really probed it. Both must remain true AFTER this capability ships — the point is that discovery is the only route to a valid quote, not that quotes stopped being checked.
ON A NON-WINDOWS HOST assert the platform-unsupported refusal arm instead, with a positive executed-case count either way. A silently skipped proof generates zero cases and passes while proving nothing, which for this task would mean shipping the capability with its central claim untested.
DoD 4 SCOPE NOTE: `apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts` belongs to task-6cbff010's slice. This task's obligation is to make a real PROVEN dispatch REACHABLE with no test-owned capability, and to say so in the completion; extending that file is the consumer's call. If you do extend it, say why and treat it as an owned path — do not edit it incidentally.

MUTATION DRILLS, GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT. Drills, each alone and reverted before the next: (1) add an optional `executablePath` to the discovery function and prefer it when present; a NAMED test must redden — this is the exact seam the withheld comment exists to keep closed, and the most plausible "convenience" regression. (2) Make ambiguous resolution pick the first candidate; the many-candidates case must redden — proving a caller who can shadow a binary on PATH cannot steer the observation. (3) Restamp one `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` refusal arm into a discovery code; a NAMED test must redden on the lost layer. (4) Re-export `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` from the barrel; the negative surface assertion must redden, proving it reads the namespace and not the file text. (5) Interpolate the resolved path into a refusal message; the message-hygiene assertion must redden. For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited — a drill that applied nothing reads as green — confirm the red lands on the INTENDED assertion, restore with `git checkout -- <file>` (never by hand), and verify `git status --short` clean before the next.
GATES, each separate with its own captured exit code: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck` exit 0; `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` reading the COUNT LINE strictly above the step-1 baseline; `pnpm typecheck` repo-wide with the path-attributed baseline — HEAD failing paths minus merge-base failing paths, intersected with your owned paths, MUST be empty. Quote any foreign red verbatim without repairing it.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW: (a) is there ANY parameter, overload, optional field or exported type through which a caller could name a binary, an fs, a facts port or a clock? (b) does resolution refuse zero and many rather than picking? (c) do all four observer refusal arms pass through with code AND layer intact? (d) does the surface comment now explain BOTH what stays withheld and why publishing discovery does not re-open the seam? (e) do the negative surface assertions still pass, read against the namespace? (f) does the real-Windows proof assert PROVEN from a real launch, with the two refusal negatives still holding? (g) does any refusal message echo a path, argv, environment value or digest? (h) is every production file under 250 lines by `grep -c ''`, the bridge one LF line? (i) does `git status --porcelain` show only owned paths with every drill reverted?
Commit by explicit pathspec — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`. Verify with `git show --stat`. In the completion: quote the count lines, name the test that reddened for each drill, state plainly that a PROVEN Claude launch is now reachable by a consumer with no test-owned capability, and record the consumers — task-6cbff010 (acceptance), task-a9fd91c3 (Foundation ingress) and task-44d4873e. Keep verification.command under 500 characters.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 7 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Publish `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` from the root. REJECTED, and the surface comment already argues it better than I could: it takes an `executablePath`, so a consumer holding it "could point the host observer at a binary no quote ever committed to". Publishing it would close this gap by re-opening the one task-75ee4a84 exists to close.

2) Let `createClaudeRuntimePinRequest` build its own quote internally. REJECTED: the factory validates the quote against a freshly observed one, so a self-built quote would make the comparison compare an observation against itself — the check would pass by construction and stop meaning anything.

3) Publish `capabilitySchemaDigestOf` and `canonicalDigest` so a caller can assemble a valid quote. REJECTED, and it is the most dangerous option because it looks like closing an information gap: those two are exactly what make a quote unforgeable. A caller able to mint the capability digest can mint a quote for a runtime nobody observed — the digest authority reimplemented outside the runner.

4) Accept an optional path hint, or an environment variable, so callers can help discovery in odd installs. REJECTED: that is the steerable argument in a new costume. Drill 1 targets it precisely because it is the most plausible "convenience" regression.

5) Pick the first candidate when host resolution finds several. REJECTED: it hands back the steering lever to anyone who can shadow a binary on PATH. Refuse ambiguity.

6) Restamp the observer's four refusal arms into one discovery code for a simpler consumer API. REJECTED: four authorities can answer, and DoD 3 requires each refusal to keep the code and layer of whichever did.

7) Extend `foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts` as part of this task. NOT PLANNED as an obligation: that file belongs to task-6cbff010's slice. This task must make a real PROVEN dispatch REACHABLE with no test-owned capability and say so; extending that file is the consumer's call, and if the worker does it they must own the path deliberately rather than incidentally.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 81a9f30. This gap is real, it was measured properly by whoever filed it (grep plus a real Windows run against claude.exe 2.1.233 on 10.0.26200), and it is the direct consequence of an asymmetry I specified in task-75ee4a84's plan. Worth saying plainly: that plan argued `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` must stay internal because publishing it "re-opens the exact authority hole the factory closes". That reasoning was right and the surface comment now states it verbatim. What the plan did not do was provide the other half — a way to OBTAIN a quote — so the factory validates against something no consumer can produce.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES SELF-ASSEMBLY IMPOSSIBLE, and shows this is not a bug to route around: `factsDigest` (claude-runtime-pin.ts:130-141) compares exactly `reportedVersion`, `adapterCapabilitySchemaDigest` and `platformIdentity{os,arch,osVersion}`, with the comment "Compares only what the runtime IS, so pinned paths may legitimately differ." The version and the capability digest can only come from an observation the runner made itself — `capabilitySchemaDigestOf` (claude-capabilities.ts:273) and `canonicalDigest` are both internal. Hence the filer's result: a quote whose closure hash and paths were ALL TRUE still refused `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_CHANGED@RUNTIME`.

THE WITHHELD LIST, confirmed at claude-surface.ts:84-92: `createNodeClaudeRuntimeFs`, `RUNTIME_PIN_CHUNK_BYTES`, `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime`, `probeClaudeRuntime`, `ClaudeRuntimeFsPort`, `ClaudeRuntimeFactsPort`, `ClaudeRuntimeObservationRefused`, and `prepareClaudeRuntimePin` ("the launcher applies it itself").

THE RESOLUTION THAT PRESERVES THE ASYMMETRY: a capability that DISCOVERS the installed runtime itself. The steerability the comment fears comes from the `executablePath` ARGUMENT, not from returning an observation. A function that names no binary — the host answers which one — hands the caller an observation without handing them the choice. That is the distinction the surface comment must be rewritten to carry, or a future reader will read the new export as the withholding having been abandoned.

NO EXISTING PUBLIC RESOLUTION: `claude-launch-selection.ts` covers launch flags, model evidence and reasoning effort (`CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_CODES`, `CLAUDE_MODEL_EVIDENCE_KINDS`, `CLAUDE_REASONING_EFFORTS`), is not published from the surface, and resolves no executable. Discovery is genuinely new.

AMBIGUITY IS THE SUBTLE STEERING VECTOR. A caller who cannot name a path may still be able to influence which candidate the host finds — PATH ordering, a shadowing install. Refusing on more than one candidate removes that lever entirely, which is why zero-and-many must both refuse rather than the resolution picking a winner. Canonicalise and de-duplicate by real path first, so one binary reachable two ways is one candidate rather than a false ambiguity.

HOST FACTS, measured earlier this session: `claude.exe` is at `C:\Users\Yaron\.local\bin\claude.exe` and the release broker is built at `dist/windows-job-native/release/moe-windows-job-broker.exe` — note that path is relative to the WORKSPACE ROOT because the gate passes `--target-dir`; `native/target/release` does not exist and reads as a false "not built".
planningNotes.risks:
1) THE STEERABLE ARGUMENT COMES BACK AS A CONVENIENCE. "Just an optional path for unusual installs" reintroduces exactly the seam the withheld comment protects. Drill 1 is the guard, and the unsteerability must be a TYPE-level fact — an absent parameter — rather than a runtime rejection one refactor from being relaxed.

2) AMBIGUOUS RESOLUTION IS A QUIETER VERSION OF THE SAME HOLE. A caller who cannot name a binary may still shadow one on PATH. Zero and many both refuse; canonicalise and de-duplicate first so a single binary reachable two ways is not a false ambiguity.

3) THE COMMENT WILL GO STALE AND MISLEAD. It currently says an observation-returning function stays internal. After this task the root publishes one. Without the rewritten distinction — discovery names no binary — the next reader concludes the withholding was abandoned and publishes the rest.

4) THE PROOF MUST BE A REAL LAUNCH. DoD 2 says PROVEN "proven by a real launch, not by a rebuilt digest". A test that reconstructs the digest would pass while proving nothing, and it is the natural shortcut when the real broker is slow.

5) THE TWO NEGATIVES MUST SURVIVE. A self-assembled quote must still refuse `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_CHANGED@RUNTIME` and a stand-in binary `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID@RUNTIME` AFTER this ships. The deliverable is that discovery is the only route to a valid quote — not that quotes stopped being checked.

6) WHOLE-OBJECT EQUALITY WOULD FAIL FOR THE WRONG REASON. `factsDigest` deliberately ignores pinned paths, so asserting the whole observation survives unchanged reddens on a legitimate difference and then gets "fixed" by loosening the assertion that matters. Assert the three compared fields.

7) MESSAGE HYGIENE. task-32eddfd3 was QA-rejected once for refusal messages echoing runtime paths; a discovery refusal naming the paths it searched leaks host layout to anyone who can trigger one.

8) `export *` HIDES A LEAK FROM GREP. Negative surface assertions must read the imported namespace; drill 4 proves they do.

9) THE EXPORT-COUNT FIXTURE WILL FAIL until updated, and that is it working — do not loosen the count.

10) A SKIPPED PLATFORM PROOF generates zero cases and passes, which here would mean shipping the capability with its central claim untested. Assert the platform-unsupported arm off Windows, with a positive executed count either way.

11) CONSUMERS: task-6cbff010 (acceptance), task-a9fd91c3 (Foundation ingress), task-44d4873e (verification receipt dispatch). All three are waiting on a reachable PROVEN launch.
